newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pioneer says reviewing Ampol stake.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pioneer says reviewing Ampol stake.

text.p: Pioneer International Ltd said on Wednesday it was reviewing its options over its stake in petroleum refiner and market, Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (Ampol).
"Pioneer is reviewing its strategic options in relation to its 50 percent interest in Ampol," Pioneer said in a commentary accompanying its half year results.
"The company has appointed the investment banks J.P. Morgan and Macquarie Bank to assist it with its review, which it expects may take several months to complete," it said.
Ampol was formed in 1995 when Pioneer and Caltex Australia combined their petroleum assets in a A$3 billion merger.

Local media reports last October speculated on the possibility of a sale of the Pioneer stake in Ampol after Pioneer reported a substantial reduction in profitability at the petrol refiner and marketer.

The reports quoted industry sources as saying the possibilities for disposal included sale through a float, a backdoor listing into Caltex, sale to Caltex's U.S. parent Caltex Petroleum Corp, and a trade sale to another party.

Caltex Petroleum is 50 percent owned by Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp. Australian Petroleum earlier reported a net profit for the year to December 31, 1996 of A$104.86 million, up from A$93.35 million previously.
Second half earnings, however, were down on the first half, due mainly to low Singapore refiner margins, Caltex said.
